# add glone alias

Add a `glone` alias that clones a repository and enters it, sparing the `cd` into a directory whose name has to be derived from the URL. The original definition:

`git clone $1 && cd (basename $1 | sed 's/.git//g')`

That is: clone, then change into the base name of the URL with the `.git` suffix stripped. It has to be a function rather than a git alias, since the `cd` must affect the interactive shell. A detail of the sketch worth keeping in mind: `sed 's/.git//g'` is unanchored and the dot is a wildcard, so a repository name containing `.git` elsewhere, or a name like `agit`, would be mangled.

- `glone git@github.com:kamilsk/dotfiles.git#v1.0.1`
- `glone git@github.com:kamilsk/dotfiles.git -- v1.0.1`
- `glone git@github.com:kamilsk/dotfiles.git at v1.0.1`
